title: Forms
summary: Forms collect user input: <form> wraps <input>, <textarea>, <select>, and a submit button. Each control needs a name so the data can be sent
learningObjectives: Apply the concept in a small program
Predict program output by reading code

sections.content: Forms collect user input: <form> wraps <input>, <textarea>, <select>, and a submit button. Each control needs a name so the data can be sent.
Input types matter: text, email, password, number, checkbox, radio, date. The type gives free validation and better mobile keyboards.
Key points: always label inputs (accessibility), required marks mandatory fields, and the form action/method decide where data goes.

sections.codeExample:
<form action="/signup" method="post">
    <label for="email">Email</label>
    <input type="email" id="email" name="email" required>
    <button type="submit">Sign Up</button>
</form>
